En 2018, les aéroports français ont accu:
In 2018, French airports welcomed 81.2 million passengers, an average of 6.76 million per month. This figure will serve as a reference to analyze the variations during and after the Covid period and to see if this crisis has had an impact on our way of travelling by air.
    We chose 2018 as the reference year because this is the last full year before we hear about the Covid

\n - Les deux visualisati:
- The following two visualisations aim to show the evolution of traffic, but by decomposing it in function of the type of connection: flights to and from metropolitan France (including Corsica), overseas territories (DOM-TOM), the European Union and destinations outside the European Union.
                - The first graph shows the evolution over the period 2018-2025 (as shown in the first curve), but by type of link.
                - The second graph shows the percentage of passengers recovered from pre-Covid levels.
                - In 2018/2019, the breakdown was as follows: EU (55%) > Non-EU (24%) > Metropolitan France (16%) > Overseas Departments and Territories (5%).
                - It is noted that flights to overseas departments and territories do not follow seasonal variations with the heatmap. These flights remain fairly stable throughout the year, unlike other types of routes.
                - Since the beginning of the confinement, domestic flights have kept the area afloat, particularly flights to metropolitan France. International flights have collapsed completely.
                - The second graph shows that while domestic flights in metropolitan France experienced the smallest decline, flights to overseas departments and territories (DOM-TOM) bounced the fastest, reaching 61% of traffic in 2018 as early as February 2021, while the rest of the sector did not exceed 16% of it. This is due to the fact that border controls remain strict for international flights and to the existence of alternative means of transport to travel in the metropolis.
                - It is nevertheless interesting to note that after the end of border controls in March 2022, flights outside the EU increased dramatically, to the point of being the first to recover their pre-crisis levels, thus exceeding those of the overseas departments and territories.
                - To answer the question of what is responsible for the decrease in numbers compared to 2018, it is domestic flights that are at fault. In 2025, the highest volume of domestic flights was 56% of those in 2018. European flights are also down to 96% of the 2018 traffic.
                - The decline in domestic flights is large enough to lead to an overall decrease in traffic, while in international and overseas departments and territories, the figures have never been higher, with an increase of 30 per cent in the number of international flights.

This analysis showed that Covid did not have a very long-term impact on the sector. The data indicate that only domestic flights experienced a decline in demand. The rest of the sector has recovered fairly quickly from this international crisis, see has benefited.

\n Le réseau de transport aérien fran:
The French air transport network is a hub centered on Paris. Some connections concentrate most of the activity.  
    This dependency is quantifiable: 13% of routes account for 50% of traffic. This is due not only to the size of the aircraft, but also to the changing mentality of societal issues such as ecology. Long-haul flights carry approximately twice as many passengers per flight.  
    The fact that the network is mainly based on a small number of routes could have a significant negative impact on the sector if one or more of these routes were to be closed for various reasons. One example that comes to mind is the closure of many links to the Middle East because of the war.

\n **Points clés** (filtres par défau:
**Key Points** (default filters, 2018 to 2025)
    - The Covid shock was important but short. Traffic fell 99.7% in April 2020 compared to 2018, and returned to normal levels from 2023.
    - The recovery is uneven. Flights in the metropolis peak at 56% of their 2018 level, while international and overseas flights exceed it.
    - The network is a hub focused on Paris airports and in particular on CDG. 13% of flights carry 50% of passengers, and long-haul flights carry approximately 1.9 times as many passengers per flight as short-haul flights.

    **Implications**
    - Dependence on a few routes and Paris makes the sector vulnerable to a new shock (sanitary, war, closure of airspace).
    - The declines observed on the recovery cannot be explained solely by the crisis of the covid. This is an interpretation.
